headline: Analysis and split choices, not just models, determine apparent performance in biological modelling
label: Evaluation Protocol Sensitivity
summary: Three preprints show that centring, recentering and trial-level splits can change or inflate conclusions about neural and biomechanical model performance.
synthesis: The common thread is that evaluation design can drive apparent model results. In EEG covariance representations, recentering removes subject identity yet leaves Riemannian RDMs unchanged, so de-identification does not imply alignment. A multiverse RSA reanalysis on THINGS fMRI shows that choices such as centring can flip whether untrained CNNs beat trained ones as V1 models. In ground reaction force estimation, trial-level splits inflate R² and cross-laboratory transfer fails under subject-held-out evaluation. The new element is the explicit treatment of protocol, whether analysis pipeline or data partitioning, as a tested variable rather than a fixed background. The GRF work addresses leakage most directly, while the RSA work addresses analytic sensitivity. All three are preprints, so the findings are preliminary.
